criteria: calibrate writes cohort on a newly recorded observation only when profile.estimate.cohort is configured and every tokens > 0 row of measurement.total.rows normalizes to exactly one known (agent, model) pair; agent_type, model_provider, model_generation and model_id come from that pair through a closed normalization table, the three policy digests from the profile, and measure_contract_version from core's constant.

An observation whose tokens > 0 rows span more than one (agent, model) pair, or contain a null or unknown agent or model, gets no cohort and is recorded eligible_for_knn false with MIXED_OR_UNATTRIBUTED_USAGE plus one fixed-template detail built only from allowlisted model keys, the literals claude / codex / null / other and integers (never a raw payload string); no rounding to a dominant model and no per-session split, asserted by tests that fail against the pre-change code.

When profile.estimate.cohort is not configured and the identity is resolved, calibrate records the observation exactly as before (no cohort, eligibility unchanged); an unresolved identity is ineligible regardless of the profile; and no observation recorded earlier is ever backfilled: the schema's never-backfilled rule stays, and a re-run whose cohort presence would differ from the existing record exits 1 without writing.

estimate/v2 treats a candidate as cohort-matched only when every cohort field equals the target's: agent_type, model_provider, model_generation or model_id differing yields MODEL_GENERATION_MISMATCH, a differing routing, prompt or execution digest or measure_contract_version yields ROUTING_PROFILE_MISMATCH, with no new reason code and no estimate/v2 contract version change.

design.md records the split rule, the no-backfill rule and the attribution scope declaration (an observation covers the sessions bound through lane work; changing that scope rotates execution_profile_digest), profiles/generic.profile.yaml stays without a cohort, and all packages/* test suites, typecheck and biome stay green.
